newsitem.title: JAPAN: IBJ says not "uncomfortable" with 124 yen/dlr rate.
newsitem.headline: IBJ says not "uncomfortable" with 124 yen/dlr rate.

text.p: The chairman of the Industrial Bank of Japan Yoh Kurosawa told reporters on Thursday that he was not "uncomfortable" with an exchange rate of 124 yen to the dollar.
He said that an exchange rate of 124 yen to the dollar "was not an uncomfortable level, but what is a concern is the turbulence".

At the same news conference, the head of economic research at Deutsche Bank in Frankfurt, Axel Siedenberg, said that meeting the criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU) would not put European currencies under downward pressure.
"There is no problem with convergence criteria on inflation rates or interest rates, and even if the debt level is high, if it is on a downward trend, that is okay," he said.
But he acknowledged that Germany does have a problem with debt.
"The percent of debt will be increasing over the next few years (due to the cost of continuing reunification with the former East Germany)," he said.
He added that "Germany and France have to participate or EMU does not make sense".
